title: Integrity sampler status and tenant verifier kit
content:
Draft customer-facing status update + self-serve verifier kit

Purpose:
- Provide a concise status entry for status.redwood.ai and a small, low-friction verifier kit customers can use to confirm whether their tenant-observed responses were affected.
- Offer clear opt-in replay / evidence steps for customers who want deeper validation.

Summary for status page (1–2 sentences):
At 2029-08-12 03:14 UTC we detected a short window of inconsistent response outputs for a subset of streaming generation requests originating from our eu-west-1 cluster. The issue was caused by a rare eviction and index race in the prefix/KV caching layer after an internal batching kernel rollout. Most requests were unaffected; impacted tenants may see truncated or misordered tokens for sessions that started in the 03:12–03:18 UTC window.

User-facing impact (concise):
- Affected surface: streamed text generations (chat and completion endpoints) during 03:12–03:18 UTC, eu-west-1 region only.
- Symptoms: partial token duplication, short runs of out-of-order tokens in otherwise valid responses, occasional premature stream end.
- Percentage of traffic: ~0.4% of streaming requests in eu-west-1 during the window.
- Data integrity: request payloads were preserved; there is no evidence of user data leakage.

What we did (high level):
- Immediately rolled back the batching kernel change and reverted the KV eviction scheduling to the previous stable policy at 03:25 UTC.
- Enabled an extra-level watch on prefix cache operations and deployed a corrective patch to guard against concurrent index rewrites at 04:10 UTC.
- Replayed a controlled set of internal test traces to validate ordering preservation and streaming continuity.

Current status:
- Service is operating normally in eu-west-1 as of 04:12 UTC.
- We continue to monitor for recurrence and have extended detailed tracing for another 72 hours.

Action for customers (choose one):
1) Quick self-check (recommended for any tenant that observed degraded outputs):
   - Use the tenant verifier UI in the Console: Console > Observability > Integrity Sampler.
   - Enter a request id or a short time range (2029-08-12 03:12–03:18 UTC) to get a digest. The verifier will: show sample streamed token sequences, compute a per-response checksum, and flag ordering anomalies.
   - If the UI shows "No anomaly detected", no further action needed.

2) Light evidence export (for engineering teams wanting raw evidence):
   - From the Console export panel, choose "Integrity export (sample)" and request a max 50-response bundle for the time range above. We'll provide: original request payloads, server-side token deltas, and canonical checksums.
   - Recommended for customers who need to cross-check against their own logs before requesting a replay.

3) Opt-in replay and reconciliation (for tenants seeking reconstruction):
   - Open a support incident with the subject: "Replay request: eu-west-1 2029-08-12 03:12-03:18" and include your tenant id and up to 3 example request ids.
   - We will coordinate a controlled replay (read-only) and provide a reconciliation package containing: replay results, mismatch report, token-level diffs, and suggested mitigation steps for application-level dedup/merge.

Why we believe the fix is safe: 
- The rollback removes the scheduling change that enabled the race. The corrective patch serializes index rewrites and enforces a short-lived write lock which prevents the interleaving observed.
- Internal replays and canary traffic show no ordering regressions across a broad set of model families and sequence lengths.

FAQ (customer-facing bits to include on status page):
Q: Could my customer-facing content be lost?
A: No — request payloads were preserved. Some streaming sessions may have produced incomplete token sequences; we provide repair guidance and replay options above.

Q: Will this change affect latency or cost?
A: The short-term protective lock may add a negligible latency tail on a tiny fraction of streaming requests; we do not expect measurable cost changes. We will roll a refined lock-free fix if needed after monitoring.

Q: Do I need to rotate keys or change auth?
A: No authentication or key rotation is required. This was an internal cache/indexing issue.

Operator notes (internal short checklist):
- [ ] Prepare status.redwood.ai entry: short summary, impact, mitigation, timeline.
- [ ] Publish Console banner with link to verifier UI and incident contact.
- [ ] Attach export button entitlements for affected tenants (auto-grant for opt-in exports).
- [ ] Customer success: proactively reach out to top 25 impacted tenants with sample evidence and an offer for a replay.
- [ ] Engineering: run extended canary across eu-west-1 for 72h and provide hourly telemetry snapshots to CS.

Suggested email snippet for proactive outreach (short):
Subject: Quick verification offer for potential eu-west-1 streamed responses (2029-08-12)
Hi <customer-name>,
We detected a small number of streamed responses that may have contained out-of-order tokens during 2029-08-12 03:12–03:18 UTC in eu-west-1. We preserved your request data and have a self-serve verifier in Console plus an optional replay. If you saw any user impact or want us to run a replay for a few example request ids, reply to this message and we'll prioritize.
Thanks,
Aisha on behalf of Redwood Customer Ops

Open questions for internal review: 
- Do we want to auto-offer a $ credit for tenants that opt into a replay? (finance/legal input)
- How long should exported evidence be retained in the tenant download bundle (default 7 days)?
- Should we tag models that participated in affected sessions to surface them in postmortem tech appendix?

Attachments (for CS use):
- Minimal verifier UI walkthrough (Console screenshots) — to be attached before publishing.
- Sample export README (commands and checksum verification steps) — draft below.

Sample export README (engineer-facing, paste into export bundle):
1) Files provided: requests.jsonl, server_tokens.jsonl, checksums.txt
2) Verify bundle integrity locally: shasum -a 256 checksums.txt | shasum -c -
3) Quick diff tool (python): run the included verify_diff.py to see token-level mismatches and suggested rollforward steps.

Next steps:
- CS to finalize status copy and run it by Legal for the liability line.
- Engineering to produce a short regression test that asserts no ordering anomalies under high-concurrency prefix rewrites.
- Revisit the lock implementation after 72h monitoring and plan refined kernel change if safe.

Notes to self: keep messaging concrete, minimize technical jargon on the public status entry, and give customers immediate, low-effort ways to validate their own signals.

(End of draft)
